title: South Savo: where a EUR 1,000,000 budget should go first on the lung cancer pathway
markdown:
# South Savo: where a EUR 1,000,000 budget should go first on the lung cancer pathway

## The gap in one sentence
The model estimates that South Savo patients wait 155 days (139–174) from first symptom to treatment start, the same as the Finnish estimate of 155 days (147–164) [^model]. The figure reported by Yle MOT for Finland is 155 days, against 107 in Sweden and 67 in Denmark [^src_yle_fi_a_74_20250979][^src_yle_fi_a_74_20242733].

## Where the days are lost
The step furthest above the national value is from first primary care contact to referral [^model]. The model estimates it at 47 days (38–58), against a measured 41 days nationally [^model]. The model links that step to GP waits: 69.7% of non-urgent GP visits wait over 7 days, against 54.7% nationally (measured) [^sotkanet_6411]. The model also links it to low continuity of care, with a COCI of 0.17 against 0.29 nationally (measured) [^sotkanet_5502]. The patient interval is the longest step at an estimated 51 days (40–65), but it is below the national 56 [^model].

## Three actions
1. **Symptom awareness campaign (cough over three weeks)**
   **What:** Tell people with a persistent cough to see a doctor, on the English "Be Clear on Cancer" model [^model].
   **Owner:** FICAN and the Cancer Society nationally, with county communications and primary care delivering locally [^model].
   **Cost:** EUR 10,518 per year, sourced from the roadmap budget; repeating it every year is an assumption [^model].
   **Expected effect:** 0 days saved and an estimated 0.37 deaths avoided per year (0.16–0.56) [^model].
   **Evidence:** In England the stage I share rose by 3.1 percentage points, in a before-after design; the regional pilot was not significant [^ev_symptom_campaign_1].
   **Roadmap:** 1.3.2, national symptom-awareness communication plan [^roadmap_1.3.2].

2. **Low-dose CT screening for long-term heavy smokers**
   **What:** Invite 50–74-year-old heavy smokers to CT, with cessation support [^model].
   **Owner:** The Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko decide, the Finnish Cancer Registry steers, and the county delivers [^model].
   **Cost:** EUR 404,432 per year (assumption) [^model].
   **Expected effect:** 0 days saved and an estimated 2.88 deaths avoided per year (2.11–3.65), arriving after years rather than within a budget year [^model].
   **Evidence:** Nine randomised trials give a pooled relative rate of 0.84 (0.76–0.92) [^ev_ldct_screening_1], and the NELSON trial gives 0.76 [^ev_ldct_screening_2].
   **Roadmap:** 2.3.4, new national screening programmes [^roadmap_2.3.4].

3. **Smoking cessation started at the first specialist visit**
   **What:** Give cessation medication and counselling to every current smoker with suspected lung cancer [^model].
   **Owner:** The chief physician and head nurse of pulmonology [^model].
   **Cost:** EUR 36,840 per year (assumption) [^model].
   **Expected effect:** 0 days saved and an estimated 0.29 deaths avoided per year (0.20–0.38) [^model].
   **Evidence:** One observational cohort found a hazard ratio of 0.67 (0.53–0.85) [^ev_smoking_cessation_at_diagnosis_1].
   **Roadmap:** 3.1.2, cancer-specific care pathways [^roadmap_3.1.2].

## What to measure from Monday
- Record the date of first symptom and of first primary care contact for each lung cancer patient; no one records these nationally today [^model].
- Record the days from referral to the first pulmonology visit for suspected lung cancer [^model].
- Record the days from first specialist visit to treatment decision, and from decision to treatment start [^model].
- Record stage at diagnosis and treatment intent [^model].

## Limits of this analysis
These are county-level estimates, not measurements of individual pathways. Each step is a national median adjusted with assumed, unfitted elasticities [^model]. Deaths avoided are modelled, not observed [^model]. None of the three top-ranked actions shortens the pathway; the full EUR 990,485 package is estimated to avoid 3.72 deaths per year (2.90–4.64) [^model].
